title: Diwali Home Makeover Ideas 2026: A Tricity Guide to a Festive Home Without Major Renovation
alt: AI interior concept based on Ruchit Residence’s mandir alcove, reimagined as an indoor pooja room with warm lighting and framed Goddess Lakshmi artwork
intro: A considered Diwali refresh can make a home feel warm and welcoming without starting a full renovation. This practical guide helps Mohali and Tricity homeowners decide what to update, what to leave, and how to plan the final weeks before the festival.
quickAnswer: For a festive home before Diwali, start with decluttering and repairs, then refresh the living room with a clear furniture layout, a few coordinated textiles and layered lighting. Style the entrance and mandir with care, keep walkways clear, and leave structural work or new electrical wiring for a properly planned project. For a home in Mohali, Chandigarh, Panchkula or Zirakpur, adapt every idea to the room’s layout, daylight and building rules.
sections: Diwali decoration ideas for home: what can you refresh before the festival?

Diwali falls on Sunday, 8 November in 2026, so the remaining time is best used for focused, lower-disruption updates rather than assuming a complete home renovation can be finished before the festival. Start with a walk-through and write down what guests will see and what your family uses every day. Fix loose handles, replace tired bulbs, clear surfaces and complete any small repairs before adding decoration. A fresh, orderly room often feels more considered than one filled with new accessories. The High Commission of India’s 2026 holiday calendar lists Diwali on 8 November; check local timings separately if you are planning religious observances.
How can I make my living room feel luxurious for Diwali?

Begin by editing the room. Remove items that do not belong, make a clear route from the entrance to the seating, and group cushions or objects in a restrained colour story. A pair of textured cushions, a clean throw, fresh flowers or one carefully chosen centrepiece can bring a festive note without replacing the furniture. Keep the coffee table usable and leave enough space around seating. If you are moving large pieces, check door swings and circulation before settling on the arrangement. A luxury feel comes from proportion, light and a few coherent details—not from adding decoration to every surface.
What lighting works well for a warm, festive home?

Use the lights you already have intentionally. General room lighting helps people move around; a table or floor lamp adds a softer pool near seating; a focused light can serve a reading or serving area. Warm-toned decorative lights can add a festive layer, but avoid glare, tangled wiring and overloaded sockets. Keep cables away from walking routes, children and pets, and use outdoor-rated products only where they are meant to be used. For permanent changes, have the electrical plan and installation checked by a qualified electrician. Our guide to layered lighting for homes explains how ambient, task and accent light serve different purposes.
How should I style a small apartment or 2BHK/3BHK?

In an apartment, use the surfaces and corners that already work instead of trying to fill every wall. Keep the balcony threshold and entry route clear, choose a small number of coordinated accents, and use vertical space only where it does not make the room feel crowded. For a 2BHK or 3BHK, repeat one or two colours across shared spaces so the home feels connected, then let bedrooms keep their own character. Check society rules before attaching lights to a balcony, facade or common area. Do not block ventilation, windows or access to fire-safety equipment for the sake of a photograph.
How can I make the entrance and mandir feel special?

A clean entrance, a working light and a simple arrangement can make a thoughtful first impression. Keep footwear, parcels and cables organised, and make sure the door opens freely. For a mandir or pooja corner, clean the niche, check the light and arrange the items your family actually uses. Add flowers or a small festive detail without overcrowding the shelf. If you light a diya, put it on a stable, non-flammable surface away from curtains, flowers, paper, children and pets, and never leave an open flame unattended. The lead image is an AI interior concept based on the mandir alcove photographed at DMS Studio’s Ruchit Residence project in Mohali. The room setting, framed Goddess Lakshmi artwork and lighting are illustrative; see the linked project page for original site photographs.
Which work should wait until after Diwali?

A new false ceiling, major carpentry, rewiring, plumbing changes, custom furniture or structural alterations need site checks, drawings, coordination and time for materials and installation. Starting them close to a festival can create dust, access problems and rushed decisions. If a home needs that level of work, use this period to define the scope and priorities, then agree a realistic programme with the designer and relevant contractors. Any schedule depends on the actual site, approvals, scope and material availability; a consultation cannot guarantee completion by a particular date.
A real Mohali project to explore

Ruchit Residence is a 400-gaj home in Phase 1, Mohali. Its project page documents the facade, living areas, storage, stair and mandir alcove shown in the photographs. Explore the Ruchit Residence project for the actual images and project context. A photograph can help you describe the atmosphere you like, while the layout and technical decisions for your home still need to be worked out for your own site.
A simple pre-Diwali home checklist

First, list the rooms and the small repairs that matter most. Next, declutter and clean before buying anything. Check bulbs, switches and decorative-light cables; plan a clear furniture route; choose a few textiles or accents that work with existing finishes; and arrange the entrance and mandir safely. Leave time to test the lights in the evening and remove anything that causes glare or blocks movement. If the list grows into new wiring, built-in storage or a room redesign, note it for a properly scoped project after the festival.
faqs: How can I decorate my home for Diwali without renovating?

Declutter first, complete small repairs, arrange the furniture for clear movement, add a few coordinated textiles, use existing lamps thoughtfully and keep the entrance and mandir simple. Avoid beginning disruptive work too close to the festival.
What are simple Diwali decoration ideas for a small flat?

Use a small number of coordinated accents, warm decorative lighting installed safely, a tidy entrance and a compact mandir arrangement. Keep the balcony, windows and circulation routes clear, and follow your housing society’s rules.
How can I make a living room look luxurious on a budget?

Edit clutter, improve the furniture layout, use a restrained colour palette, refresh a few textiles and add light at more than one height. A carefully styled focal point usually feels calmer than many unrelated accessories.
Which lights should I use for Diwali at home?

Combine comfortable general room lighting with a lamp for a softer pool and suitable decorative lights for the festive mood. Check product instructions, keep cables out of walkways, avoid overloaded sockets and ask a qualified electrician about permanent electrical changes.
Can a full home renovation be completed before Diwali?

It depends on the site, scope, approvals, design decisions, material availability and contractor schedule. Major work should not be promised on a short deadline without checking those dependencies. A designer can discuss a realistic programme after reviewing the project.
Does DMS Studio provide interior design in Mohali and Tricity?

DMS Studio is based in Mohali and works across Mohali, Chandigarh, Panchkula, Zirakpur, Kharar and New Chandigarh. Contact the studio to discuss your home, location, priorities and suitable project scope.
seo: Diwali home makeover ideas for Mohali and Tricity: festive living-room styling, safe lighting, mandir decor and simple refreshes without major renovation.

title: A home that feels like you: start with the way you live
alt: Personal living room with leather sofa and greenery — editorial photograph
intro: The most personal rooms begin with the way you live. A useful design brief connects routines, storage and the things you want to keep before it settles on a style.
quickAnswer: Start an interior brief with the people who use the home, their daily routines, room-by-room storage needs, existing furniture, priorities, budget range and timing. Add a few visual references and explain what you like about each.
sections: Map an ordinary day

Think through a weekday from the front door to bedtime. Where do keys, shoes and bags land? Who uses the kitchen at the same time? Is the living room mostly for family evenings, visitors or quiet work? These ordinary moments reveal circulation and storage needs that a style board cannot. Write down the friction points too: a crowded entrance, a desk with poor light or a cabinet that cannot hold what it was built for. The goal is not to design around every passing habit. It is to notice the routines that happen often enough to shape the plan.
Separate needs from preferences

Make two short lists. The first covers what must work: clear routes, accessible storage, a place to study, enough seating or a kitchen that supports the way you cook. The second covers the feeling you want: calm, bright, warm, expressive or restrained. Both lists matter, but they answer different questions. Function sets the brief; colour, finish and furniture help express it. If family members want different things, note the difference early so the design conversation can find a considered balance.
Choose references with a reason

A small, edited set of images is more useful than a large folder with no notes. Beside each reference, write what attracted you: the soft light, the uncluttered wall, the storage detail or the mix of materials. The reason can be carried into a different room even when the exact furniture or dimensions cannot. Include examples you dislike as well, with a note explaining why. This gives a designer a clearer picture of your taste and helps prevent an attractive image from becoming an unrealistic instruction.
Bring existing facts into the conversation

Share the current floor plan if you have one, a few photographs of the space, the property location, furniture you plan to keep and any known electrical or plumbing constraints. Mark anything uncertain. A drawing helps a first discussion, but it is not a measured survey; final joinery and site work need dimensions checked at the property. Add a working budget range and important dates so the scope can be discussed honestly. A useful brief makes assumptions visible instead of hiding them until work begins.
Learn from a compact-home example

Opera Home is a documented 1BHK apartment on Kurali Road, Mohali, coordinated remotely for an NRI client. Its project notes describe a bohemian direction, practical storage and a layout planned for a compact footprint. The useful lesson is not to copy a particular colour or piece of furniture. It is to decide what the available space needs to do, then use a consistent visual language to make those functions feel connected. The project page shows the actual DMS photographs and identifies the limits of what they document.
What should I include in an interior design brief?

Include the location and property type, a plan or current photographs, the people who will use the space, room-by-room priorities, storage needs, furniture to retain, a working budget range, timing constraints and a few annotated visual references. Note what is known and what still needs a site check. These details help an interior designer prepare a focused first conversation; they do not replace a measured survey or a written project scope.
faqs: Do I need to know my exact style before contacting a designer?
No. Share the rooms that need attention, how you use them and a few images with notes about what appeals to you. The visual direction can be developed during the design conversation.
Should I send a floor plan?
If you have one, it is a useful starting reference. Final dimensions and site conditions should still be verified before detailed planning or fabrication.
Can an interior design brief include a budget range?
Yes. A working range helps the team discuss priorities and scope. A final proposal should clarify inclusions, exclusions and assumptions in writing.
seo: Learn how to brief an interior designer: organise routines, room priorities, storage, budget and visual references before planning a home in Mohali.

title: Layered lighting for homes: ambient, task and accent light
alt: Table lamp and plants illustrating a quiet layer of light — editorial photograph
intro: A comfortable lighting plan supports different activities through the day. Start with daylight and the room layout, then give each light source a clear job.
quickAnswer: Layered lighting combines general ambient light, focused task light and selective accent light. Plan each around the room’s use, daylight, furniture and glare control; coordinate electrical installation with qualified professionals.
sections: Begin with daylight and the room

Notice when direct sunlight enters and how the room is used after dark. Windows, curtains, wall colour and reflective finishes all affect how bright a space feels. Look at material samples in the actual room when possible: a pale finish can read differently under morning daylight and warm evening lamps. Record where glare falls on a screen, mirror or glossy surface. This simple observation gives the lighting plan context before any fixture is chosen.
Use ambient light for general orientation

Ambient light is the broad, comfortable illumination that helps people move through and use a room. It can come from ceiling fixtures, concealed sources or a combination of fittings. The right arrangement depends on the ceiling, room proportions and activities; there is no universal fixture count that fits every home. Aim for even enough coverage for ordinary use while avoiding a harsh pool of light directly overhead.
Plan task light where work happens

Task lighting supports a specific activity: reading, food preparation, grooming or focused desk work. Decide where that activity will happen, then coordinate the light with the furniture and work surface. In a kitchen, check where the person stands and whether upper cabinets cast a shadow over the counter. Beside a bed, consider whether one person needs to read while another rests. Switch placement and glare control matter as much as the fixture itself.
Use accent light with restraint

Accent light draws attention to a surface, artwork, niche or architectural detail. It can add depth, but too many competing highlights make a room feel restless. Choose one or two features that deserve attention and check how they look from the main seating and circulation routes. Concealed lighting should be planned with access for maintenance and a clear understanding of what it will illuminate. A strip light that is visible from every angle may distract more than it helps.
Coordinate the layers before installation

Review the furniture plan, ceiling design, switch locations and finish samples together. Consider how lights will be controlled in scenes for cooking, working, entertaining and winding down. Electrical loads, wiring and installation should be checked by qualified professionals against the actual property conditions and applicable requirements. A design image can communicate atmosphere, but it does not specify a circuit, fixture rating or safe installation detail.
What are ambient, task and accent lighting?

Ambient lighting provides general room illumination; task lighting supports an activity such as reading or cooking; accent lighting highlights a chosen feature. A well-planned room may use all three, arranged around how people move and work rather than a fixed number of fixtures.
A project to study: Babbar Residency

Babbar Residency in Sector 125, Mohali, documents a 3BHK home with custom woodwork, a feature wall and ceiling lighting. View its project photographs to see how the studio’s chosen light and finishes appear together. Those images show a particular completed space; they do not establish the electrical specification or fixture quantity for another home. Use them as a conversation reference, then plan your room from its own layout and site conditions.
faqs: Should I select lights before furniture?
Plan them together. Furniture establishes where people read, cook, work and gather; the lighting plan can then serve those activities and the room’s circulation.
Is warm light always best for a home?
Not in every location or task. Consider the activity, surrounding finishes and desired atmosphere, and review samples in the space before confirming a specification.
Can a lighting photo be used as an electrical plan?
No. A photograph can illustrate an idea, but circuiting, wiring, fixture ratings and installation need a project-specific plan prepared and checked by qualified professionals.
seo: Understand ambient, task and accent lighting, and how to plan home lighting around daylight, furniture, daily routines and glare.

title: Before hiring an interior designer: questions for the first meeting
alt: Materials and brushes on an artist’s worktable — editorial photograph
intro: You do not need every answer before speaking with an interior designer. Bring a clear starting point and use the conversation to understand scope, process and responsibilities.
quickAnswer: Before your first interior design meeting, gather the property location, available plan, current photos, room priorities, working budget and timing. Ask what the proposed scope includes, what happens next and how changes are documented.
sections: Bring the essentials

Share the property location and type, a floor plan if available, and photographs of the current rooms. Note whether the home is occupied, newly handed over, under construction or being renovated. List the rooms you want to change and the ones that already work. This helps a designer understand the context before suggesting a direction. If measurements are approximate, say so; an early plan should not be mistaken for a site-verified drawing.
Describe the outcome you need

A useful brief explains what should improve, not only what style you like. Perhaps the entry needs storage, the kitchen needs a clearer work sequence, or a salon needs a more comfortable waiting area. Share the people who use the space, equipment or furniture that must remain, and any known building rules. Prioritise the changes as essential, preferred or optional. That makes trade-offs easier to discuss if the scope needs to fit a budget or programme.
Ask for a written scope

Clarify whether the proposal covers design, drawings, material selection, procurement, contractor coordination, site visits, installation or styling. Ask what the studio supplies and what is handled by you or a separate specialist. Confirm how professional fees, taxes, delivery, appliances, site preparation and changes are treated. A headline price is difficult to compare without the same scope and assumptions. Request a written outline before committing so both sides can refer to the same expectations.
Discuss decisions, approvals and timing

Ask how concepts are presented, who approves selections and how revisions are recorded. Discuss the sequence of design decisions and what information is needed before work begins. A start or completion date depends on the agreed scope, site readiness, approvals, material availability and other project conditions. A responsible conversation identifies these dependencies instead of promising a fixed timeline before the details are known.
Agree on a practical next step

At the end of the meeting, ask whether the next action is a site visit, measured survey, proposal, concept package or another discussion. Find out what you should provide and when the studio will respond. If you are comparing multiple providers, use the same property information and ask each one to describe inclusions and exclusions clearly. You can then compare the approach, scope and communication rather than relying on a presentation alone.
A commercial example: Essentia Salon

Essentia Salon in New Chandigarh is a DMS commercial interior project. Its project page documents the salon’s storefront and interior spaces. For a salon brief, questions about client arrival, waiting, treatment stations, staff movement, product display, storage and cleaning can help shape the planning conversation. The actual layout and services for another salon would still need a site review and an agreed scope; one project is an example, not a ready-made specification.
How can I compare interior design proposals fairly?

Compare proposals against the same rooms, drawings and project assumptions. Check design deliverables, materials, quantities, procurement, installation, specialist work, taxes, delivery, site visits and change handling. Ask for exclusions and responsibilities in writing. This creates a clearer comparison than looking at a single total without understanding what it covers.
faqs: Should I have a fixed budget before the first meeting?
A working range is helpful, even if it may change. Discuss priorities and scope openly, then ask for a written proposal that explains its assumptions and exclusions.
Can I ask an interior designer for a guaranteed completion date?
Ask how the programme is developed and what it depends on. Dates should be discussed against scope, site readiness, approvals and supply conditions rather than promised without those details.
What documents should I bring?
Bring a plan if available, current photographs, the property location, a list of priorities, known building requirements and any material or furniture references you want to discuss.
seo: Prepare for an interior design consultation with a practical checklist for project scope, budget, timing, approvals and comparing proposals.
metaTitle: First Interior Design Meeting Checklist | DMS Studio

title: How to plan a 3BHK interior in Mohali before choosing finishes
alt: Bright residential interior illustrating a calm, practical home-planning palette — editorial photograph
intro: A 3BHK home is easier to plan when the family’s routines, storage and circulation are resolved before selecting finishes. This sequence can help organise an early design brief.
quickAnswer: For a 3BHK interior, first confirm the measured plan and site conditions. Then plan shared-room circulation, kitchen workflow, bedroom storage, lighting and the budgeted scope before finalising materials or decorative details.
sections: Start with a verified plan

Use the builder or existing plan as a reference, then check dimensions, columns, doors, windows, service points and ceiling conditions at the property before detailed decisions. Mark which information is confirmed and which needs a site visit. This is particularly useful in an apartment, where plumbing, electrical points and building rules may constrain changes. Do not treat a marketing plan or an approximate sketch as a fabrication drawing.
Give the shared rooms a clear sequence

Map the route from entry to living, dining, kitchen and bedrooms. Note where household members cross paths, where visitors sit and where daily items accumulate. A living room may need to serve family time and guests; the dining area may also become a work surface. Test furniture layouts on paper before adding partitions or feature elements. Clear walking space often makes a room feel more generous than extra furniture does.
Plan each bedroom for its user

A bedroom needs more than a bed and wardrobe. Ask who uses it, what should be stored, whether a study or dressing area is required and what furniture will stay. Check wardrobe door movement, bedside access, daylight, curtains and charging points together. A child’s room may need a layout that can adapt as interests and study needs change. A guest room may require flexible storage. These uses should be decided before finalising joinery and finishes.
Coordinate kitchen, lighting and storage

Confirm appliance dimensions and the preparation, washing, cooking and storage sequence before cabinet sizes are finalised. Check how drawers and doors open beside each other. Plan task lighting where work happens, general light for movement and switches that are convenient on arrival. Measure storage needs instead of estimating cabinet volume from a photograph. Final services and electrical work should be reviewed for the specific property by qualified professionals.
Separate scope from styling

Write down what the project includes: planning, drawings, kitchen or wardrobe work, ceiling and lighting, finishes, procurement, installation and any specialist services. Agree a working budget and note exclusions, taxes, delivery, appliances and site preparation. Once these are clear, select a palette that supports the layout and the home’s daylight. A calm material direction can connect rooms without making every room identical.
Project context from Mohali

TDI Wellington is a documented 3BHK apartment project in Sector 117, Mohali. Its portfolio page shows the living and dining area, connected kitchen and other rooms using supplied project imagery. Treat the photographs as evidence of that project’s visible decisions, not as a plan for a different apartment. The dimensions, building rules, family routines and service points of your own home should shape its design.
What should be planned first in a 3BHK interior?

Confirm the site measurements and building constraints first. Then plan circulation, room use, storage, furniture and kitchen workflow. Coordinate lighting and services with that layout before choosing final finishes and decorative details.
faqs: Can a 3BHK plan be prepared before possession?
Early planning can start from available drawings and a design brief, but measurements and site conditions should be checked after access is available and before detailed execution decisions.
Should all three bedrooms use the same design?
They can share a coherent overall palette while responding to different users, storage needs, daylight and activities.
Does a project photograph show the exact materials and dimensions?
It documents what is visible in a particular project. Confirm specifications and dimensions for your own property rather than inferring them from a photograph.
seo: Planning a 3BHK interior in Mohali? Use this room-by-room guide to coordinate layout, storage, kitchen workflow, lighting and finishes.

title: Kids’ bedroom design: make a football theme work beyond the mural
alt: Thoughtful family-home interior used as editorial inspiration for adaptable room planning
intro: A themed children’s room can feel personal without making every surface permanent. Plan the practical layout first, then use colour, graphics and accessories to express the child’s interest.
quickAnswer: Keep a child’s bedroom adaptable by making storage, study lighting, circulation and bed placement the long-term foundation. Use replaceable elements—art, bedding, accessories and a focused feature wall—to express a football theme.
sections: Begin with sleep, study and movement

List the activities the room must support: sleeping, dressing, reading, homework, play and storing sports equipment. Measure the bed, desk and wardrobe, then check clear routes between them. Keep frequently used items accessible and avoid placing storage where it blocks doors, windows or natural light. If the room is shared, identify each child’s storage and study needs separately before combining the layout.
Choose which elements carry the theme

A football theme can come through a mural, a graphic, bedding, framed prints, colour accents or a display for a favourite ball or jersey. Choose one main feature and a small number of supporting details so the room still feels restful. Permanent joinery can stay simple and useful; softer items are easier to change as a child’s interests evolve. Discuss the scale and position of graphics with the child so the feature feels intentional rather than crowded.
Make storage easy to use

Think about what needs a home: school books, clothes, toys, shoes, sports gear and seasonal items. Low shelves and labelled drawers can make everyday tidying more approachable. Use closed storage for items that tend to make the room feel visually busy, while keeping a few meaningful objects visible. The internal layout of a wardrobe matters as much as its exterior: hanging, folded clothes and drawers need different arrangements.
Give study and bedtime separate light

A desk benefits from focused light positioned to reduce shadows and screen glare. General room lighting supports movement and getting dressed; a softer bedside source can make reading more comfortable. Plan switches and sockets with the furniture position in mind, and have electrical requirements checked by a qualified professional. Curtains or blinds should also be considered alongside daylight and sleep routines.
Keep the room adaptable

Children grow, and their storage, study and display needs change. Leave space for a larger desk or different furniture where the plan allows. Keep the foundation—bed access, storage and safe circulation—useful even if a mural or colour palette changes. Choose finishes that can be maintained in daily use and avoid treating a theme as a fixed identity the child must keep for years.
A DMS project example: Evaan Joshi’s bedroom

The Evaan Joshi case study documents a children’s bedroom designed around a young football fan. Its photographs show a football mural, blue-and-white palette, themed bedding, study desk and coordinated storage. These project details are visible in the case study; other rooms will have different dimensions and family needs. Use the example to discuss how a child’s interest can guide colour and imagery while the room still serves sleep, study and storage.
How can a football bedroom stay stylish as a child grows?

Keep permanent furniture and storage practical, and use changeable items such as bedding, prints and accessories to express the theme. A single feature wall can make the room feel personal without making every future update expensive.
faqs: Should a football mural cover every wall?
Usually a focused wall or graphic gives the theme a clear place without overwhelming the room. Choose its position after planning the bed, desk and main sightlines.
How can I plan storage for a child’s room?
List clothes, school items, toys and sports equipment separately, then assign accessible storage to everyday items and higher or closed storage to occasional-use belongings.
Can the room be designed for a child’s future needs?
Yes. Keep the core layout flexible, allow for changing study needs where possible, and use replaceable decor for interests that may change.
seo: Plan a football-themed kids’ bedroom with practical storage, study lighting and adaptable decor inspired by a DMS Studio project in Mohali.

title: Salon interior design: plan the customer journey and work zones
alt: Commercial interior lighting detail used as editorial inspiration for salon planning
intro: A salon layout has to support a calm client experience and a workable staff routine. Map how people move through the space before choosing finishes or styling stations.
quickAnswer: Plan a salon from the client journey and staff workflow: entrance, reception, waiting, consultation, service stations, storage, cleaning and exit. Check equipment dimensions, utilities, privacy and maintenance before finalising the interior layout.
sections: Trace the client journey

Begin at the entrance and follow what a visitor does next: where they are greeted, where they wait, how they reach a service station and how they leave. Make reception easy to find without blocking the doorway. Give waiting guests a clear place to sit and consider what they can see from that position. A useful layout makes the next step feel natural without using signs to solve every circulation problem.
Plan staff movement and work surfaces

Map the repeated tasks performed at each station. Check the space needed for a stylist or technician to work, for a client to sit comfortably and for equipment to be placed within reach. Keep staff routes between stations, storage and cleaning areas in mind. If different services need different equipment or privacy, plan their zones accordingly. The layout should work when the salon is busy, not only when the room is empty for a photograph.
Coordinate services and maintenance

List the equipment, power, water, ventilation and storage requirements that the salon team actually uses. Confirm dimensions and service points before cabinetry is detailed. Choose finishes that suit the expected cleaning routine and discuss maintenance access for lights, mirrors and equipment. Electrical, plumbing and ventilation decisions must be checked for the specific premises by qualified professionals and against building requirements.
Use lighting for tasks and atmosphere

A salon needs clear light for detailed services and a comfortable atmosphere for clients. Consider mirrors, reflective finishes, daylight and how skin or hair colour appears in the space. Avoid glare in mirrors and direct light that makes waiting uncomfortable. General lighting, task lighting and decorative accents should be coordinated rather than chosen as isolated fixtures. Confirm technical requirements with the relevant lighting and electrical professionals.
Make the brand visible through the space

Colour, texture, signage and furniture can express the salon’s identity, but the first responsibility is a layout that supports service. Decide where the brand should be most visible: entrance, reception, display, or a backdrop that appears in photographs. Product displays need clear sightlines and simple restocking. Avoid treating every wall as a feature; a calmer background can help the business’s work and people stand out.
Essentia Salon, New Chandigarh

The DMS Studio Essentia Salon case study documents the supplied storefront and salon interior photographs. Its page presents the project’s client-facing environment and interior details. Use those images to discuss how a real salon’s arrival, waiting, display and service zones relate to one another. The photographs do not reveal hidden services, exact dimensions or equipment specifications, so any new salon requires its own measured plan and operations brief.
What should a salon interior brief include?

Include the premises plan, services offered, equipment list, staff workflow, expected waiting needs, storage and cleaning requirements, utility points, building rules, budget and opening timeline. Confirm the technical details on site before finalising drawings.
faqs: What should be planned first in a salon?
Start with the services provided and map the client journey and staff workflow. Then coordinate stations, equipment, storage and utilities around that operating plan.
How do I avoid glare at salon mirrors?
Review fixture placement from the client and staff positions, test mirror reflections and confirm the lighting arrangement in the actual space before installation.
Can I copy a salon layout from a project photo?
A photo is a visual reference, not a measured plan. Use it to explain preferences, then adapt the design to your premises, equipment and service workflow.
seo: Plan a salon around client flow, staff zones, treatment stations, lighting, storage and building services. See the Essentia Salon project.

title: Interior design ideas for every room in a Mohali home
alt: Editorial living room with natural textures and greenery; not a DMS Studio project
intro: Good interior ideas begin with how each room is used. Use these room-by-room prompts to plan a coherent home without copying one look everywhere.
quickAnswer: Start with a measured plan and the daily use of each room. Give the entry a clear landing place, the living room comfortable circulation, bedrooms practical storage, and the kitchen a workable route between preparation, cooking and cleaning. Choose finishes after those decisions, then connect the rooms with a consistent material and lighting direction.
sections: Begin with the entry, not the feature wall

The first few steps inside a home shape how the rest of it works. Decide where shoes, keys, bags and deliveries will go. A shallow cabinet or a small shelf can be more useful than a large decorative console when the passage is narrow. Check that the door opens fully and that stored items do not spill into the route to the living room.
Make the living room fit real conversations

Place seating around the people who use it, then check clear walking space to doors and balconies. Test furniture dimensions on the actual plan before buying a sofa or building a media wall. Use more than one light source so the room supports family evenings, guests and quieter moments. In Babbar Residency, Sector 125, Mohali, the photographed green wall and mustard seating show a strong visual idea within a family living space; the layout for another home should still start with its own measurements.
Give each bedroom a purpose

A bedroom should accommodate the bed, movement around it, everyday clothes and the specific needs of its user. Plan wardrobe access with the door fully open and check where switches, charging points and bedside light will sit. A guest bedroom may need flexible storage; a child’s room benefits from furniture that can adapt as routines change. The Evaan Joshi bedroom is one documented DMS example of a theme combined with study and storage.
Plan the kitchen around work, not just finish

Before selecting shutter colours, mark the sink, hob, refrigerator, preparation surface and storage on a verified plan. Consider who cooks, whether two people work together and where groceries arrive. Check appliance clearances, ventilation and service access. The cabinet construction, hardware and moisture details matter as much as the visible finish. For more specific decisions, see DMS Studio’s kitchen, storage and lighting service.
Use light and storage to connect the rooms

A consistent home does not require every room to use the same colour. Repeat a few related materials or tones, then adjust the lighting for each activity. Keep frequently used items near where they are needed, and reserve closed storage for visual clutter. Layer general, task and accent light where useful; permanent wiring should be planned and installed by a qualified professional.
Take the ideas back to the actual property

Photographs can suggest a mood, but they cannot confirm a wall dimension, an electrical point or the condition behind an existing finish. Bring your floor plan, site photographs, priorities and the rooms you want to address to the first design discussion. DMS Studio’s completed project portfolio offers real visual references; the exact scope and specification for your home should be agreed separately.
faqs: What should I plan first when designing several rooms?
Start with a measured plan and a brief for the people using each room. Resolve circulation, storage and essential services before finalising decorative finishes.
Should every room have the same interior style?
No. A small shared material or colour direction can make rooms feel connected while each room responds to its own light, size and daily use.
Can DMS Studio plan multiple rooms and execute the work?
DMS Studio discusses residential design and turnkey execution around the property and proposed scope. Share your plan and priorities so responsibilities and deliverables can be confirmed.
